verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:
verses.commentary: 15:1 "Son of man" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SON OF MAN.

verses.zh: 「人子啊，葡萄树比别样树有甚么强处？葡萄枝比众树枝有甚么好处？
verses.en: “Son of man, of all the woody branches among the trees of the forest, what happens to the wood of the vine?[NOTE:1]
notes: Most modern translations take the statement as a comparison (“how is vine wood better than any forest wood?”) based on the preposition מִן (min). But a comparison should have a word as an adjective or stative verb designating a quality, i.e., a word for “good/better” is lacking. The preposition is translated above in its partitive sense.sn Comparing Israel to the wood of the vine may focus on Israel’s inferiority to the other nations. For the vine imagery in relation to Israel and the people of God, see Ps 80:8-13; John 15:1-7; Rom 11:17-22.
verses.commentary:
15:2 "how is the wood of the vine better" The vine is often used as a symbol of Israel (cf. Ezek. 19:10; Ps. 80:8-16; Isa. 5:1-7;
Hosea 10:1; Rom. 11:17-22). In this brief parable Judah and Jerusalem are given to Neo-Babylon for the burning (cf. Ezek. 19:12; 23:25; Jer. 21:10;
32:28-29; 39:8; 52:13; 2 Chr. 36:19).

Grapevines are not good fuel for cooking because they burn too hot and too quickly! It is also too soft to be used for furniture or
construction. One cannot even make a tent peg out of vine wood! It is useless except for producing fruit, but Israel did not produce (cf. Deut. 32:32; Isa. 5:1-7; Jer. 2:21)!

The prophets often symbolized idolatry as an imported vine (cf. Isa. 17:10; Ezek. 8:17).

The personification of trees is not unusual in the OT. Note Jdgs 9:7-15! Parables and riddles are common ways for eastern people to
express themselves. In reality chapters 15, 16, and 17 form this genre of literature.

verses.zh: 其上可以取木料做甚么工用，可以取来做钉子挂甚么器皿么？
verses.en: Can wood be taken from it to make anything useful? Or can anyone make a peg from it to hang things on?

verses.zh: 看哪，已经抛在火中当作柴烧，火既烧了两头，中间也被烧了，还有益于工用吗？
verses.en: No![NOTE:1] It is thrown in the fire for fuel; when the fire has burned up both ends of it and it is charred in the middle, will it be useful for anything?
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) draws one’s attention to something. Sometimes it may be translated as a verb of perception; here it is treated as a particle that fits the context (so also in v. 5, but with a different English word).
verses.commentary:
15:4 "fuel. . .consumed" There are two terms (the NOUN, lit. "food," BDB 38 and the VERB,
BDB 37, KB 46) which form a wordplay found only in Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 15:4,6; 21:32).

▣ "fire" See SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE.

verses.zh: 完全的时候尚且不合乎甚么工用，何况被火烧坏，还能合乎甚么工用么？」
verses.en: Indeed! If it was not made into anything useful when it was whole, how much less can it be made into anything when the fire has burned it up and it is charred?

verses.zh: 所以，主耶和华如此说：众树以内的葡萄树，我怎样使它在火中当柴，也必照样待耶路撒冷的居民。
verses.en: “Therefore, this is what the Sovereign Lord says: Like the wood of the vine is among the trees of the forest that I have provided as fuel for the fire—so I will provide the residents of Jerusalem[NOTE:1] as fuel.[NOTE:2]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
The words “as fuel” are not in the Hebrew text but are implied.
verses.commentary:
15:6 "give" The VERB (BDB 678, KB 733, Qal PERFECT) is used twice in this
verse and again in Ezek. 15:7 and 9. YHWH's judgment of Jerusalem is sure.

verses.zh: 我必向他们变脸；他们虽从火中出来，火却要烧灭他们。我向他们变脸的时候，你们就知道我是耶和华。
verses.en: I will set[NOTE:1] my face against them—although they have escaped from the fire,[NOTE:2] the fire will still consume them! Then you will know that I am the Lord, when I set my face against them.
notes: The word translated “set” is the same Hebrew word translated as “provide” in the previous verse.
This escape refers to the exile of Ezekiel and others in 597 b.c. (Ezek 1:2; 2 Kgs 24:10-16).
verses.commentary:
15:7 "I set (lit. "give") My face against them" See note at Ezek. 14:8. This phrase also appears in the Levitical passage on
covenant disobedience (i.e. covenant curses for disobedience, cf. Lev. 26:17), which is alluded to three times in this chapter (and often in Ezekiel).

▣ "Though they have come out of the fire, yet fire will consume them" If they (i.e. the inhabitants of Jerusalem) escape
one of the four judgments of YHWH, another will get them (cf. 1 Kgs. 19:17; Isa. 24:18; Amos 9:1-4).

It is possible that this refers to the first two groups of Judeans who were exiled in 605 and 597 B.C. and who
were currently in Babylon. They are the potential repentant remnant that YHWH will begin again with (cf. Ezek. 6:7-9; 14:22-23).

verses.zh: 我必使地土荒凉，因为他们行事干犯我。这是主耶和华说的。」
verses.en: I will make[NOTE:1] the land desolate because they have acted unfaithfully, declares the Sovereign Lord.”
notes: The word translated “make” is the same Hebrew word translated as “provide” in v. 6.
verses.commentary:
15:8 "I will make the land desolate" "Desolate" (BDB 1031) is a recurrent threat in Jeremiah
(15 times) and Ezekiel (21 times). This threat is first stated in the curses of Lev. 26:33 and reiterated by Isaiah (6 times).

▣ "acted unfaithfully" This VERB (BDB 591, KB 612, Qal PERFECT) is first
used in Ezek. 14:13 (see note there) and 17:20; 18:24; 20:27; 39:29. The term is mentioned specifically in the penalties for covenant
disobedience in Lev. 26:40. It does not appear in Isaiah or Jeremiah. In Ezek. 20:27 the covenant people had a history of disobedience starting from
the Exodus (i.e. Exodus 32; Neh. 9:16-32) and continuing.

This parable's imagery sets the literary stage for Jesus' condemnation of Israel in His day (cf. Matt. 21:33-46; Mark 12:1-12;
Luke 20:9-19)! I have come to believe that Jesus' Olivet Discourse, Paul's "man of lawlessness" text, and John's book of Revelation all
refer to the fall of Jerusalem in A.D. 70. Please look at my exegetical verse-by-verse commentaries on these texts (free online).

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing
is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 15:1-8

1Then the word of the Lord came to me, saying, 2"Son
of man, how is the wood of the vine better than any wood of a branch which is among the trees of the forest? 3Can wood be taken from it to
make anything, or can men take a peg from it on which to hang any vessel? 4If it has been put into the fire for fuel, and the fire has consumed
both of its ends and its middle part has been charred, is it then useful for anything? 5Behold, while it is intact, it is not made into anything. How much
less, when the fire has consumed it and it is charred, can it still be made into anything! 6Therefore, thus says the Lord God,
'As the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so have I given up the inhabitants of Jerusalem; 7and I set My
face against them. Though they have come out of the fire, yet the fire will consume them. Then you will know that I am the Lord, when I set My face against them.
8Thus I will make the land desolate, because they have acted unfaithfully,'" declares the Lord God.
